university-uni-01.title: Deposit by lunch or lose the room
university-uni-01.prompt: You find a near-perfect apartment close to campus. The “landlord” says another student is ready to take it and asks for one month’s deposit by bank transfer before lunch, promising a video tour afterward.
university-uni-01.answersA: Do not send money before verifying the property, landlord and lease; use an in-person/verified viewing or trusted rental platform process.
university-uni-01.answersB: Ask the university housing office or a local contact to help verify the address and landlord before paying.
university-uni-01.answersC: Send a smaller holding deposit first so the landlord keeps the room while you verify.
university-uni-01.explanation: Rental scams rely on scarcity and distance. A smaller irreversible transfer is still an irreversible transfer.
university-uni-01.proTip: Housing pressure is real; proof of control comes before payment.

university-uni-02.title: Your tuition refund closes today
university-uni-02.prompt: An email says your university overcharged tuition and a refund must be claimed by 5 p.m. The link opens a university-looking page asking for your student login and bank details.
university-uni-02.answersA: Contact the bursar/student finance office through a known university channel.
university-uni-02.answersB: Use the link because the email includes your student ID and exact program name.
university-uni-02.answersC: Open the student finance portal from the university website you already use and check for the refund there.
university-uni-02.explanation: Student details are often available from compromised accounts or public sources. Refunds should appear in the institution’s own finance system.
university-uni-02.proTip: A refund is not urgent enough to borrow someone else’s login page.

university-uni-03.title: Easy remote job, start tonight
university-uni-03.prompt: A recruiter texts you about a remote “data optimization” job paying daily. You can start tonight by rating products in an app. After a few small payouts, the app says you must deposit your own money to unlock higher-paying tasks.
university-uni-03.answersA: Deposit only enough to complete one more task so you can withdraw the larger balance.
university-uni-03.answersB: Stop; do not deposit money. Verify the employer independently and report/block the job contact.
university-uni-03.answersC: Withdraw any funds you legitimately can without paying more, then stop using the platform.
university-uni-03.explanation: Task scams often show fake earnings and may pay a little first to build trust before demanding deposits.
university-uni-03.proTip: A job that requires you to pay to unlock pay is not a job.

university-uni-04.title: Accept your award in 60 minutes
university-uni-04.prompt: A scholarship email says another candidate will receive your award if you do not accept within 60 minutes. Acceptance requires a $25 “identity processing” fee and a photo of your student ID.
university-uni-04.answersA: Verify the award through the scholarship organization’s official site and your university financial-aid office before paying or uploading ID.
university-uni-04.answersB: Ask for formal award terms and whether the fee can be deducted from the scholarship rather than paid upfront.
university-uni-04.answersC: Pay the small fee to reserve the award, then verify before sending the ID.
university-uni-04.explanation: Scarcity plus congratulations can bypass skepticism. Legitimate awards should be independently verifiable before money changes hands.
university-uni-04.proTip: Winning should create funding, not a payment emergency.

university-uni-05.title: Visa status: respond before midnight
university-uni-05.prompt: An email says a change in immigration rules means your student status needs “immediate reconfirmation” before midnight. The form asks for your passport, visa document and current bank balance.
university-uni-05.answersA: Save the message and ask a designated school adviser to review it before submitting anything.
university-uni-05.answersB: Upload the documents now because immigration deadlines can be strict, then confirm tomorrow.
university-uni-05.answersC: Use the immigration authority’s official site and your university international office to verify whether any action is actually required.
university-uni-05.explanation: Fear of losing legal status creates extreme urgency. Sensitive immigration documents should move only through verified government/university channels.
university-uni-05.proTip: Immigration fear is exactly why the channel must be verified.

university-uni-06.title: Student section, half price, ten minutes
university-uni-06.prompt: A student-group account offers last-minute sports tickets at half price and says the transfer window closes in ten minutes. Payment must be sent by a peer-to-peer app before the ticket is transferred.
university-uni-06.answersA: Send half now to hold the seat and the rest after transfer.
university-uni-06.answersB: Use a ticket platform with verified transfer/buyer protection or skip the deal.
university-uni-06.answersC: Ask for a live screen recording of the ticket inside the official ticket app and verify the seller independently.
university-uni-06.explanation: Short windows create fear of missing out and encourage irreversible payment. Transaction protection matters more than student affiliation.
university-uni-06.proTip: Campus identity is not buyer protection.

university-uni-07.title: Your laptop delivery needs $2.40
university-uni-07.prompt: You are waiting for a new laptop when a text says the courier needs a $2.40 redelivery fee before 3 p.m. The message includes a tracking number that looks similar to your real one.
university-uni-07.answersA: Check the order and tracking in the retailer/carrier app or website you open yourself.
university-uni-07.answersB: Contact the carrier independently if the tracking status is unclear.
university-uni-07.answersC: Pay the small fee because the delivery timing and tracking number are close enough.
university-uni-07.explanation: Expected high-value packages make delivery phishing particularly believable. Tiny fees can be bait for card and identity data.
university-uni-07.proTip: Expected package, unexpected payment path: verify.

university-uni-08.title: Emergency grant expires tonight
university-uni-08.prompt: A social post says students affected by rising living costs can claim an emergency grant tonight. The application asks for your banking login so the “grant engine” can verify financial need automatically.
university-uni-08.answersA: Ask student services or financial aid whether the program is legitimate.
university-uni-08.answersB: Apply if the grant is widely shared by students, but change your bank password afterward.
university-uni-08.answersC: Check your university, government or recognized aid provider directly for the grant; never give a grant form your banking login.
university-uni-08.explanation: Real hardship creates real urgency, which makes fake aid persuasive. Financial verification does not require handing over online-banking credentials.
university-uni-08.proTip: Aid applications may ask for documents; they do not need your bank password.

university-uni-09.title: Professor needs an assistant today
university-uni-09.prompt: An email that appears to come from a professor says a research assistant dropped out and they need someone today. The job pays well and begins with depositing a check to buy equipment from a “preferred vendor.”
university-uni-09.answersA: Deposit the check but wait for it to show as available before buying the equipment.
university-uni-09.answersB: Verify the job with the professor or department through a separate university channel before depositing anything.
university-uni-09.answersC: Ask for the position to be posted through the university’s normal hiring system.
university-uni-09.explanation: Fake checks can appear available before they are later reversed. The professor identity and purchasing process must be verified first.
university-uni-09.proTip: “Funds available” is not the same as “check cleared.”

university-uni-10.title: Summer sublet needs a deposit now
university-uni-10.prompt: A student says they are leaving for the summer and will sublet their room cheaply. They send a video tour and student ID photo but need a deposit tonight because “three exchange students are asking.”
university-uni-10.answersA: Verify the person, property and permission to sublet through the landlord/building or trusted university housing process before paying.
university-uni-10.answersB: Arrange a live video call showing the person at the property and verify the lease/sublet rules.
university-uni-10.answersC: Pay a smaller deposit because the student ID and video make the listing likely genuine.
university-uni-10.explanation: IDs and property videos can be stolen from real listings. Payment should follow proof that the person controls the right to rent the space.
university-uni-10.proTip: A room video proves the room exists, not that the sender can rent it to you.

university-uni-11.title: “Immigration officer” says stay on the line
university-uni-11.prompt: A caller says your visa record has a mismatch and that leaving the call could trigger enforcement. They know your nationality and university and ask you to verify identity with passport details and a payment.
university-uni-11.answersA: Write down the name, case number and agency, then verify them independently before sharing anything.
university-uni-11.answersB: Stay on the line but refuse payment until they email from an official government domain.
university-uni-11.answersC: End the call and contact the immigration authority and your university international office through official channels.
university-uni-11.explanation: Government impostors use fear, specific personal data and isolation. Real authorities can be verified outside the incoming call.
university-uni-11.proTip: If an official says you may not hang up, that is a reason to hang up.

university-uni-12.title: Your professor’s “quick favor”
university-uni-12.prompt: An email from a professor’s display name says they are in a conference session and need you to buy gift cards for visiting speakers. They promise reimbursement from the department tomorrow.
university-uni-12.answersA: Buy the cards but do not send the codes until the professor confirms later.
university-uni-12.answersB: Verify with the professor or department through a known channel before buying anything.
university-uni-12.answersC: Ask for the request to go through normal university purchasing or an administrator.
university-uni-12.explanation: Authority plus helpfulness can bypass normal controls. Gift-card requests should still follow university purchasing rules.
university-uni-12.proTip: A professor’s title does not suspend procurement.

university-uni-13.title: Campus police says you owe a fine
university-uni-13.prompt: A caller claiming to be campus police says a complaint was filed about your online activity and you can avoid a formal disciplinary referral by paying an administrative fine today.
university-uni-13.answersA: End the call and contact campus police/student conduct through official university numbers.
university-uni-13.answersB: Ask for the case number and written notice in your student portal before taking action.
university-uni-13.answersC: Pay if they accept a normal card and send a university-branded receipt.
university-uni-13.explanation: Professional payment methods and branding do not authenticate an authority demand. Verify the case in the institution’s own system.
university-uni-13.proTip: Real discipline leaves a real institutional trail.

university-uni-14.title: Registrar says your account is on hold
university-uni-14.prompt: An email says a registration hold will cancel your classes unless you verify identity today. It links to a page asking for your student login and a photo of your passport or driver’s licence.
university-uni-14.answersA: Ask your adviser or student services whether identity verification is required.
university-uni-14.answersB: Use the link because losing your classes would be a bigger risk than uploading ID.
university-uni-14.answersC: Open the registrar/student portal directly and check for a hold there; contact the registrar through a known channel if needed.
university-uni-14.explanation: High-consequence academic threats make phishing powerful. A genuine hold should exist in the student system you already use.
university-uni-14.proTip: If it can cancel your classes, it should appear in the real portal.

university-uni-15.title: “Federal loan relief” has your balance
university-uni-15.prompt: A caller says they work with a government student-loan relief program and correctly quotes your approximate balance. They can lower payments if you provide your loan account login and pay an enrollment fee.
university-uni-15.answersA: Pay the fee if the quoted balance matches your real debt, since that suggests database access.
university-uni-15.answersB: Use the official loan servicer/government portal to check eligibility and never hand an incoming caller your account login.
university-uni-15.answersC: Ask for the program name and verify it independently with your loan servicer or financial-aid office.
university-uni-15.explanation: Loan balances can be obtained through breaches or data brokers. Eligibility should be verified through the actual loan system.
university-uni-15.proTip: Knowing your debt does not make someone your lender.

university-uni-16.title: Your student bank account is “under review”
university-uni-16.prompt: A caller ID shows your bank name. The caller says unusual transfers triggered a review and asks you to approve a login notification so they can inspect the account.
university-uni-16.answersA: Deny the prompt, hang up, and contact the bank through its app or the number on your card.
university-uni-16.answersB: Freeze transfers/cards in the bank app first, then call the bank yourself.
university-uni-16.answersC: Approve once because the caller ID matches and the approval is only for inspection.
university-uni-16.explanation: MFA approval authorizes account access; it is not a view-only inspection tool.
university-uni-16.proTip: A security prompt is a door, not a support ticket.

university-uni-17.title: IT is “migrating” your mailbox
university-uni-17.prompt: A Teams message from “University IT” says your mailbox is being migrated and asks you to approve a Microsoft login and then authorize a new “Mail Transfer” app.
university-uni-17.answersA: Check whether a migration notice exists on the university IT status page before doing anything.
university-uni-17.answersB: Approve the login but refuse the app if its permissions look too broad.
university-uni-17.answersC: Deny the request and contact IT through the official help desk or portal.
university-uni-17.explanation: A malicious OAuth app can access mail and files without stealing your password. Migration language makes broad permissions seem normal.
university-uni-17.proTip: IT changes should be visible in IT’s real status channel.

university-uni-18.title: The property manager changed the rent account
university-uni-18.prompt: Your building manager emails that rent must go to a new bank account after a “payment processor migration.” The message includes your unit number and the manager’s usual signature.
university-uni-18.answersA: Send a small test payment first to make sure the account works.
university-uni-18.answersB: Confirm the new bank details through the tenant portal or a known phone number before changing your payment.
university-uni-18.answersC: Ask for the change to be posted in the formal tenant system or lease communication.
university-uni-18.explanation: A test transfer proves only that the destination receives money. Payment-detail changes are a classic point for independent verification.
university-uni-18.proTip: Verify the owner of the account, not its ability to receive money.

university-uni-19.title: Big-name recruiter wants documents now
university-uni-19.prompt: A recruiter claiming to represent a well-known company offers you a remote interview. Before scheduling it, they ask for a driver’s licence, tax number and bank details “to pre-clear onboarding.”
university-uni-19.answersA: Verify the recruiter and role through the company’s official careers site or HR contact before sharing sensitive information.
university-uni-19.answersB: Ask to interview first and provide only the information normally needed at that stage.
university-uni-19.answersC: Send the ID but hold back bank details until after the interview.
university-uni-19.explanation: Real employers may need identity and payroll data after hiring, not before they have established a genuine process.
university-uni-19.proTip: Hiring should get more specific before your data gets more sensitive.

university-uni-20.title: Campus health says coverage will lapse
university-uni-20.prompt: A message claims to be from the university health plan and says your coverage lapses tomorrow unless you re-enter insurance and payment details. It includes the correct semester dates.
university-uni-20.answersA: Check your current coverage status in the insurer portal before entering anything.
university-uni-20.answersB: Use the link because the semester dates and university logo are correct.
university-uni-20.answersC: Open the university health-insurance portal directly or contact student health through a known channel.
university-uni-20.explanation: Public academic calendars make timing easy to imitate. Coverage status should be verified in the actual account.

university-uni-21.title: Your roommate’s payment handle changed
university-uni-21.prompt: Your roommate messages from their usual account: “My payment app is locked—send your share of rent to this new handle tonight.” The amount is exactly what you owe.
university-uni-21.answersA: Pay because the amount and timing match your real rent arrangement.
university-uni-21.answersB: Verify the change in person or by calling the roommate on a known number before sending money.
university-uni-21.answersC: Ask the landlord whether your share can be paid directly through the normal rent channel instead.
university-uni-21.explanation: Compromised accounts inherit real history and timing. A changed payment destination is the moment to verify the person.
university-uni-21.proTip: Correct amount, wrong destination is still a loss.

university-uni-22.title: The study guide asks for your login
university-uni-22.prompt: A classmate posts a “professor-approved” study guide in the group chat. The link asks you to sign in with your university account and approve access to your files and contacts.
university-uni-22.answersA: Ask for the file through the university’s normal drive/LMS and do not approve broad access.
university-uni-22.answersB: Verify with the classmate or professor through another channel before connecting your account.
university-uni-22.answersC: Approve it because the classmate is real and everyone needs the guide for the exam.
university-uni-22.explanation: The classmate’s account may be compromised, and broad OAuth access is unnecessary for a simple document.
university-uni-22.proTip: A study guide should not need your inbox or contacts.

university-uni-23.title: Your new campus friend has a “sure thing”
university-uni-23.prompt: A student you met through an international-student group is friendly and helpful. After several weeks they introduce you to a crypto platform that supposedly helped them cover tuition and offer to coach you through it.
university-uni-23.answersA: Check whether the platform is regulated/recognized where you live and whether withdrawals are independently reported.
university-uni-23.answersB: Try a small amount first and continue only if you can withdraw it successfully.
university-uni-23.answersC: Do not invest through a platform introduced by a new relationship; research independently and seek advice from someone you already trust.
university-uni-23.explanation: Investment scams often build relationships first and may allow small withdrawals to deepen trust.
university-uni-23.proTip: A helpful person can still be leading you into an unhelpful platform.

university-uni-24.title: Can you receive this for me?
university-uni-24.prompt: A student you know from class says their bank account is temporarily frozen and asks whether a €900 “scholarship reimbursement” can be sent to you. They want you to keep €50 and forward the rest to another account once it arrives.
university-uni-24.answersA: Help once because you know the student in real life and you can wait until the €900 appears in your account before forwarding it.
university-uni-24.answersB: Decline to receive or forward the money and suggest they resolve the payment through their bank or the university’s official finance office.
university-uni-24.answersC: Ask the university finance office or your bank whether there is any legitimate reason for a scholarship payment to pass through another student’s account.
university-uni-24.explanation: Receiving and forwarding money for someone else can pull you into fraud or money-mule activity even when the incoming balance initially looks real.
university-uni-24.proTip: Your bank account is not a favour-routing service.

university-uni-25.title: The date becomes a trading mentor
university-uni-25.prompt: Someone you met on a dating app near campus chats with you for weeks, then mentions a relative who trades crypto. They offer to help you make a small trade on a platform they use.
university-uni-25.answersA: Keep the relationship separate from investing and do not fund or connect a wallet based on their recommendation.
university-uni-25.answersB: Research the platform and discuss it with a financially knowledgeable person you trust before doing anything.
university-uni-25.answersC: Try a small amount first so you can judge whether the platform is real.
university-uni-25.explanation: Romance-investment scams are designed to feel like personal advice, not a sales pitch. Small early wins can be part of the setup.

university-uni-26.title: Treasurer needs a new payment account
university-uni-26.prompt: A club treasurer messages that the club’s bank account is temporarily frozen and asks members to send event payments to a personal account so the booking is not lost.
university-uni-26.answersA: Ask for the payment change to be posted in the club’s official channel with adviser approval.
university-uni-26.answersB: Pay because you know the treasurer personally and the event deadline is real.
university-uni-26.answersC: Verify the change with another officer/adviser and use the club’s approved payment process before sending money.
university-uni-26.explanation: A known person can have a compromised account or make an unsafe shortcut. Organizational payment controls protect everyone.
university-uni-26.proTip: Knowing the treasurer does not authenticate a new bank account.

university-uni-27.title: The alumni mentor wants to “help your credit”
university-uni-27.prompt: An alumnus you met through a networking group offers to help you build credit by adding you to a special financial account. They need your ID, social-security/tax number and a small setup fee.
university-uni-27.answersA: Share only the ID first because the mentor came through a legitimate university group.
university-uni-27.answersB: Do not provide the data; verify the person and any financial product independently through regulated providers or university career/alumni channels.
university-uni-27.answersC: Ask for the product name and written terms, then review them with a trusted financial adviser or family member.
university-uni-27.explanation: Real networks can be used to manufacture trust. Identity data should not be exchanged for vague financial shortcuts.
university-uni-27.proTip: A warm introduction does not make a financial product safe.

university-uni-28.title: Your friend is “stuck at immigration”
university-uni-28.prompt: A friend studying abroad messages that immigration officers are holding their passport and they need you to pay a “release fee” to a third party. The account contains years of your real conversations.
university-uni-28.answersA: Contact the friend through another channel and, if necessary, verify with their family, university or consulate before sending money.
university-uni-28.answersB: Ask for the name of the authority and case details, then verify them independently.
university-uni-28.answersC: Pay because the long message history proves the account belongs to your friend.
university-uni-28.explanation: A compromised account includes all the old history that makes the emergency believable.
university-uni-28.proTip: Chat history proves the account had a past—not who controls it now.

university-uni-29.title: Your lab partner shares a “new analysis tool”
university-uni-29.prompt: A lab partner sends a link to a new AI analysis tool and says the professor wants everyone to connect their university drive before tomorrow’s meeting. The app asks for full file and email access.
university-uni-29.answersA: Use a test file or separate non-sensitive account if the tool can be evaluated without real research data.
university-uni-29.answersB: Approve access because your lab partner is trusted and the meeting is tomorrow.
university-uni-29.answersC: Verify with the professor/lab lead and request the approved tool link through a known university channel before granting access.
university-uni-29.explanation: Compromised collaborators and overbroad OAuth permissions can expose research, email and personal files.
university-uni-29.proTip: A new tool should prove its need before you grant old data.

university-uni-30.title: The textbook seller has mutual friends
university-uni-30.prompt: A seller in a campus marketplace offers a nearly new textbook at half price. You have several mutual friends, but they want payment by bank transfer before meeting because “too many buyers no-show.”
university-uni-30.answersA: Send a small deposit because mutual friends make the profile trustworthy.
university-uni-30.answersB: Meet in a safe public place and pay after inspecting the book, or use a platform with buyer protection.
university-uni-30.answersC: Ask a mutual friend whether they actually know the seller and arrange an in-person exchange.
university-uni-30.explanation: Mutual connections can come from compromised or lightly vetted accounts. Payment protection matters more than social proximity.
university-uni-30.proTip: Mutual friends are context, not escrow.

university-uni-31.title: The check “cleared”—buy the laptop
university-uni-31.prompt: A new employer mails you a check for $2,800 to buy a laptop and software. Your banking app shows the funds as available, and the recruiter sends a specific vendor account for the purchase.
university-uni-31.answersA: Do not buy anything; verify the employer independently and wait for the bank to confirm the check is genuinely settled.
university-uni-31.answersB: Contact your bank and explain the job/check situation before moving any of the funds.
university-uni-31.answersC: Buy only the laptop amount and leave the rest untouched until the first paycheck.
university-uni-31.explanation: Fake checks can appear available before being reversed. Sending money to the “vendor” can leave you owing the bank.
university-uni-31.proTip: Available funds are not proof the check is good.

university-uni-32.title: Install this app for your interview
university-uni-32.prompt: A recruiter schedules a video interview but says the company uses a private conferencing tool. The installer asks for screen recording, accessibility control and a system password.
university-uni-32.answersA: Ask for a browser-based or mainstream alternative until the tool can be verified.
university-uni-32.answersB: Install it because companies often use specialized interview software, then uninstall afterward.
university-uni-32.answersC: Verify the recruiter and software through the company’s official careers/IT information before installing anything.
university-uni-32.explanation: Deep device permissions can expose passwords and files. A legitimate employer can explain and verify its interview tooling.
university-uni-32.proTip: The interview should evaluate you, not gain admin access to your laptop.

university-uni-33.title: The shared document wants OAuth
university-uni-33.prompt: A link to a “group project board” asks you to connect your university account and approve permission to read email, files and calendar data. The login page itself is genuine Microsoft/Google.
university-uni-33.answersA: Approve because the login page is genuinely Microsoft/Google, so your password is safe.
university-uni-33.answersB: Do not approve broad permissions; use an approved university tool or ask the sender to share the document normally.
university-uni-33.answersC: Review the app publisher and permissions with university IT before connecting it.
university-uni-33.explanation: OAuth scams can use a real provider login screen while asking you to grant a malicious app powerful access.
university-uni-33.proTip: A real login page can still authorize a bad app.

university-uni-34.title: Pay $60 to unlock $480
university-uni-34.prompt: A remote-work app shows you earned $480 from simple rating tasks. To withdraw it, the app says your account is “negative” and you must deposit $60 in crypto to complete the final task set.
university-uni-34.answersA: Do not deposit more money; stop and report the platform/contact.
university-uni-34.answersB: Try to withdraw without paying and preserve screenshots/evidence for your bank or reporting agency.
university-uni-34.answersC: Deposit the $60 because the app already paid you a small amount earlier and the visible balance is much larger.
university-uni-34.explanation: Task scams use fake balances and sometimes real small payouts to make later deposits feel logical.
university-uni-34.proTip: Never pay money to unlock wages.

university-uni-35.title: Upload passport for “student verification”
university-uni-35.prompt: A site offering student discounts asks you to upload your passport and a selfie because your university email “could not be verified automatically.” The offer is attractive but the service is unfamiliar.
university-uni-35.answersA: Ask whether a less sensitive proof of enrollment can be used instead.
university-uni-35.answersB: Upload the documents if the discount is valuable and the site uses HTTPS.
university-uni-35.answersC: Use a recognized student-verification provider or verify the offer with the merchant before uploading identity documents.
university-uni-35.explanation: HTTPS protects the connection, not the legitimacy of the recipient. Identity data should be proportional to the benefit and provider trust.
university-uni-35.proTip: A discount should not require an identity package from a stranger.

university-uni-36.title: The free coffee QR on campus
university-uni-36.prompt: A sticker on a campus café table says students get a free drink by scanning a QR code. The page asks for your university login and then prompts for an MFA approval.
university-uni-36.answersA: Approve the MFA prompt because the QR is physically inside the café.
university-uni-36.answersB: Do not log in; ask café staff whether the promotion and QR code are theirs.
university-uni-36.answersC: Navigate to the café/university promotion page independently if one exists.
university-uni-36.explanation: Attackers can place stickers on real tables. Physical placement does not authenticate the digital destination.
university-uni-36.proTip: Real café, fake sticker is still fake.

university-uni-37.title: Approve to “restore your mailbox”
university-uni-37.prompt: After receiving an IT-looking email, you get several login prompts on your phone. A follow-up message says the prompts are part of mailbox recovery and asks you to approve the next one.
university-uni-37.answersA: Deny the prompts and contact university IT through the official help desk; change your password if compromise is possible.
university-uni-37.answersB: Use your account’s security page to review and terminate unknown sessions before calling IT.
university-uni-37.answersC: Approve one prompt to stop the repeated notifications, then change your password.
university-uni-37.explanation: Repeated prompts are often an attempt to wear down resistance. Approval gives the attacker the access they are asking for.

university-uni-38.title: The buyer “accidentally overpaid”
university-uni-38.prompt: You sell a desk in a student marketplace. The buyer sends a screenshot showing they paid $250 instead of $50 and asks you to return $200 to a different payment handle immediately.
university-uni-38.answersA: Tell the buyer to cancel/reverse the original transaction through the payment service.
university-uni-38.answersB: Refund once the screenshot shows “Completed,” because keeping the money would be wrong.
university-uni-38.answersC: Check your actual payment account and do not send a separate refund unless the original payment is genuinely settled and reversible through the provider.
university-uni-38.explanation: Screenshots can be forged and incoming payments may later reverse. Your account ledger is stronger evidence than the buyer’s image.

university-uni-39.title: Your first job is receiving packages
university-uni-39.prompt: A work-from-home employer gives you the title “Logistics Quality Coordinator.” Packages arrive at your apartment; your job is to inspect them, remove old labels and reship them to new addresses.
university-uni-39.answersA: Continue for one pay cycle because legitimate remote logistics jobs can involve repackaging.
university-uni-39.answersB: Stop and verify the employer; do not reship goods, and seek advice/report the job if items have already arrived.
university-uni-39.answersC: Keep the packages unopened while you contact the carrier or appropriate authority for guidance.
university-uni-39.explanation: Reshipping schemes can involve goods bought with stolen payment information, leaving you in the middle of the fraud.
university-uni-39.proTip: A job that turns your home into a forwarding hub deserves immediate scrutiny.

university-uni-40.title: The “credit check” needs your bank login
university-uni-40.prompt: A landlord says too many students send fake credit reports, so you must prove affordability through a link that connects directly to your bank account using your online-banking credentials.
university-uni-40.answersA: Use a recognized tenant-screening method or provide appropriate documents through a verified landlord/platform; do not enter banking credentials into an unknown link.
university-uni-40.answersB: Ask the landlord to use a reputable screening service and verify the property before sharing financial data.
university-uni-40.answersC: Connect the bank because read-only financial verification is common and faster than sending statements.
university-uni-40.explanation: Bank-connect services can be legitimate, but only when the property, landlord and provider are independently verified. An unknown link is not enough.
university-uni-40.proTip: Verify the rental before verifying your finances.

university-uni-41.title: Your exam resit slot expires in an hour
university-uni-41.prompt: A text claiming to be from the exams office says your resit slot will be released to someone else in one hour unless you secure it now with a payment to a listed account.
university-uni-41.answersA: Pay quickly to the account in the text to keep the slot.
university-uni-41.answersB: Check the resit booking directly through the official student portal instead of the link in the text.
university-uni-41.answersC: Pay, and also forward the message to classmates so they don't lose their slots either.
university-uni-41.explanation: Exam administration doesn't run through a one-hour countdown to a payment account named in a text - a real resit booking lives in the student portal.
university-uni-41.proTip: Anything that decides your academic record happens in the official portal, not a text link.

university-uni-42.title: Claim your conference travel grant today
university-uni-42.prompt: An email says you've been awarded a travel grant for a conference, but funds release today only, and you must confirm your bank details through a linked form before the deadline passes.
university-uni-42.answersA: Contact your department directly to confirm the grant is real before entering any bank details.
university-uni-42.answersB: Fill in the form, and also share it with a labmate who might want a grant.
university-uni-42.answersC: Fill in the form quickly to receive the funds today.
university-uni-42.explanation: Genuine grant administration doesn't collect bank details through a same-day emailed form - a real award goes through your university's finance office.
university-uni-42.proTip: A grant you didn't apply urgency to shouldn't come with urgency attached to it.

university-uni-43.title: Academic misconduct panel - respond in 24 hours
university-uni-43.prompt: An email says a plagiarism report has been filed against you and you must log in to a portal within 24 hours to submit your defense or be marked as non-responsive.
university-uni-43.answersA: Log in through the link right away to respond in time.
university-uni-43.answersB: Check the sender's address and confirm through your official student email or advisor before clicking anything.
university-uni-43.answersC: Log in and enter your student credentials without checking the link first.
university-uni-43.explanation: Academic misconduct processes are handled through your university's own systems and known contacts, not a rushed 24-hour email with an external portal link.
university-uni-43.proTip: A real accusation survives you checking it through a channel you already trust.

university-uni-44.title: Your device isn't compliant - install this profile
university-uni-44.prompt: A pop-up while on campus Wi-Fi says your laptop isn't compliant with university security policy and you must install a configuration profile immediately to keep network access.
university-uni-44.answersA: Ignore the pop-up and check with university IT directly through their known help desk.
university-uni-44.answersB: Install it, and also grant it full admin permissions when asked.
university-uni-44.answersC: Install the profile right away to keep working.
university-uni-44.explanation: A configuration profile can give an attacker deep control over your device. Universities don't push mandatory installs through a browser pop-up on public Wi-Fi.
university-uni-44.proTip: IT changes to your device come from IT you contacted, not a pop-up that contacted you.

university-uni-45.title: The premium AI study tool everyone's using
university-uni-45.prompt: A classmate shares a link in your course group chat to a 'premium' AI study tool that's helped everyone with exam prep - you just need to sign in with your university account to get access.
university-uni-45.answersA: Sign in since a classmate already vouched for it.
university-uni-45.answersB: Sign in, and also share the link further in the group chat.
university-uni-45.answersC: Check whether the tool is officially supported before signing in with your university login.
university-uni-45.explanation: Signing into a third-party site with your university credentials can hand that site your whole student account, even when the recommendation comes from someone you trust.
university-uni-45.proTip: A classmate's endorsement doesn't make your university login safe to hand to a random site.

university-uni-46.title: Be a paid campus ambassador for our trading app
university-uni-46.prompt: A friendly senior student says their trading app pays a bonus for every classmate you sign up as a campus ambassador, and shows you a screenshot of their own quick profits.
university-uni-46.answersA: Sign up just to see how it works before recruiting anyone.
university-uni-46.answersB: Decline, and be cautious of any offer that pays more for recruiting people than for the product itself.
university-uni-46.answersC: Sign up and start recruiting classmates right away.
university-uni-46.explanation: A program that rewards recruiting more than it rewards the underlying product is a hallmark of pyramid and affiliate-fraud schemes, regardless of who is presenting it.
university-uni-46.proTip: If the real payout is recruiting people, the product is the excuse.

university-uni-47.title: Your scholarship overpaid you - return the balance
university-uni-47.prompt: Your account shows a scholarship deposit far larger than expected. An email says it was a processing error and asks you to wire back the difference today to avoid losing the scholarship entirely.
university-uni-47.answersA: Wire back the difference today to keep the scholarship.
university-uni-47.answersB: Spend some of it first, since it's already in your account.
university-uni-47.answersC: Contact the financial aid office directly to confirm the deposit before sending any money back.
university-uni-47.explanation: Scholarship overpayment scams rely on students trusting an unexpected deposit; the real fix for an aid-office error never requires you to wire money out first.
university-uni-47.proTip: A financial aid office fixes its own mistakes - it doesn't need you to wire money to do it.

university-uni-48.title: Log in to the university portal to confirm your details
university-uni-48.prompt: An email link opens a login page that looks exactly like your university's portal, asking you to confirm your username and password after a routine security check.
university-uni-48.answersA: Log in since the page looks identical to the real portal.
university-uni-48.answersB: Log in, and also complete the 'security question' fields it asks for afterward.
university-uni-48.answersC: Check the web address carefully or type the university's URL in yourself instead of using the link.
university-uni-48.explanation: A pixel-perfect copy of your university's login page is exactly what credential phishing looks like - the giveaway is almost always the web address, not the design.
university-uni-48.proTip: A login page you reached by typing the address yourself is safer than one a link opened for you.
